**Setup.** With $\hbar^2/2m^* = 0.0380998/0.067 = 0.56865$ eV nm², define $k=\sqrt{E/0.56865}$ (well/contacts) and $\kappa=\sqrt{(0.30-E)/0.56865}$ (barriers). For a symmetric double barrier, $T=1$ exactly when the round-trip phase in the well is a multiple of $2\pi$: $kL + \arg r = n\pi$, where the single-barrier reflection amplitude is
$$r = \frac{-i\,\alpha\sinh\kappa b}{\cosh\kappa b + i\beta\sinh\kappa b},\quad \beta=\frac{\kappa^2-k^2}{2k\kappa}.$$
This gives the lowest resonance condition
$$kL = \frac{\pi}{2} + \arctan\!\big(\beta\tanh\kappa b\big),\qquad L=5\ \text{nm},\ b=2\ \text{nm}.$$
(For $b\to\infty$ this reduces to the even-state finite-well condition $\tan(kL/2)=\kappa/k$, as a check.)
